message.reasoning_content:
The process survived the shell call (PPID=1, detached). Good. http_code=200, size=13 = len("p6-service-ok"). 

Now verify with headers, and also test 404, then stop.

Then stop: kill PID, verify not listening / process gone.

Also verify from a separate later call that the service was alive across calls — the ps output already shows it running before curl in the same call... Actually the ps and curl were in the same call. Point 3 requirement is just curl. But to demonstrate background survival, the ps in the second call (separate invocation) shows it running — pid was started in call 1, and ps in call 2 confirmed alive. Good.

Now do a headers check plus stop.

function.name: shell
function.arguments:
{"command": "cd /home/rimuru/Projects/Code/for_fun/TeamAgents/review/eval/r2-p6/runs/2026-09-24-formal/work/service-check.C.2
echo "--- headers ---"
curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8765/health
echo "--- 404 route check ---"
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w 'http_code=%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8765/nope
echo "--- stopping service ---"
PID=$(cat service.pid)
kill "$PID"
for i in $(seq 1 20); do kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 0.2; done
if kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; then echo "still alive, sending SIGKILL"; kill -9 "$PID"; sleep 0.5; else echo "process $PID exited"; fi
kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null && echo "STILL RUNNING" || echo "confirmed stopped"
echo "--- curl after stop (expect failure) ---"
curl -sS -m 3 http://127.0.0.1:8765/health; echo "curl_exit=$?"
echo "--- port check ---"
(ss -ltnp 2>/dev/null || netstat -ltnp 2>/dev/null) | grep 8765 || echo "port 8765 not listening""}
